classification.difficultyReason: Decompose the floor plan into the original shed and extension, infer the extension height x+10, and model the total area before solving.

content.prompt: A $100\text{ m}^2$ hay shed is to be extended to give $475\text{ m}^2$ of floor space in total. Find the value of $x$.

spec.description: Unshaded concave L-shaped floor plan. The original upper-left 10 m square is marked by an area arrow and a red dashed right boundary. Matching double ticks identify the inner vertical and bottom horizontal sides as equal.
spec.mathematics: Original area 100 m²; extension rectangle has sides x and x+10 metres; total area 475 m².
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens only; extension dimensions are not supplemented with solution labels.

answer.worked:
The extension is a rectangle of width $x$ and height $x+10$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}100+x(x+10)&=475\\x^2+10x-375&=0\\(x+25)(x-15)&=0\\x&=-25\text{ or }15.\end{align*}$$
Since $x>0$, $x=15\text{ m}$. Check: $100+15(25)=475\text{ m}^2$.
